summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue fell to INR1,527 crores (H1 INR3,118 crores, down ~11%) as international execution stalled; FY27 guidance held at up to 10% growth.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR1,527 crores against INR1,749 crores a year earlier, with H1 down about 11% on lower international revenue (INR165 crores vs INR929 crores). Domestic EPC grew about 13% in H1 and O&M rose 48% in H1 to INR183 crores. Profit after tax was INR17 crores in Q2 versus a loss of INR478 crores a year ago, which included a one-time U.S. arbitration impact. Management said eight new projects (4 India, 4 overseas) have slowed because PPAs and financing delayed NTPs, and it expects Q3 to beat H1 and Q4 to be the strongest quarter.

segments.name: Domestic EPC
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR2,768 crores, up about 13%; Q2 domestic EPC revenue INR1,366 crores. Domestic margins under pressure from aggressive bids by new entrants.

segments.name: International EPC
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR62 crores; H1 INR165 crores vs INR929 crores. Older projects in South Africa, Spain and Italy completed; order book INR5,538 crores across Egypt and South Africa, with execution starting in H2.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR99 crores (up about 55%), H1 INR183 crores (up 48%). Portfolio at a record 18.9 GW vs 13.5 GW in March; Q2 gross margin about 23%, guided to around 20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at up to 10%; management later said this is roughly 10% and excludes Reliance orders, after an analyst noted the earlier range was 10-15%.
Q3 FY27 expected to be clearly better than H1; Q4 expected to be the strongest quarter.
EPC gross margin guided at 8% to 10%, depending on turnkey vs balance-of-system mix; O&M gross margin around 20%.
Full-year operational EBITDA margin of at least 4% to 4.5% described as a minimum requirement; recurring overheads expected at around 4.5% of revenue in FY27.
O&M revenue expected to exceed INR400 crores in FY27; O&M portfolio expected to reach 22-25 GW by year-end.
Order book expected to remain above INR10,000 crores at end FY27; over INR3,000 crores of new credit lines secured.
Around INR156 crores expected under indemnity from promoters in the current year.
capex_capacity: Eight projects (4 India, 4 overseas) in order book have not started because NTPs are delayed; management expects domestic projects to start within 1-2 months and substantial PSU revenue in Q4.

West Minya project in Egypt: 1,000 MW AC solar plus 600 MWh storage, about USD 560 million, executed via 50:50 JV with Hassan Allam Construction; NTP received, roughly 14-month duration, with Q4 expected to be heavily loaded.
Tilaiya floating solar project (Jharkhand, NTPC-DVC JV) nearing completion; power evacuation awaits state transmission line.
Won 616 MW South Africa turnkey BESS (two 308 MW projects) from a Middle East developer; LOA received; second-largest utility-scale battery project for the company.
Reliance Kutch integrated renewable hub: site readiness underway, work expected post-monsoon; management said orders expected this quarter but would not give a size or date.
demand_pricing: H1 FY27 order inflow INR3,626 crores, nearly 90% international; order book INR12,481 crores at 30 Sep 2026 (India INR6,943 crores, 56%; international INR5,538 crores, 44%), up from INR11,813 crores in March 2026.
Solar bid pipeline (excluding BESS) grew to 34 GW from 27.7 GW last quarter; about 74% India and 26% overseas. Solar and storage bidding opportunities of INR45,000-50,000 crores expected in H2.
Domestic ALMM-II cell mandate since June 2026: compliant modules scarce and costly, possibly raising project costs 15-17%; domestic cell capacity about 35 GW vs over 200 GW module capacity.
Management cited aggressive low-priced bids by new entrants in reverse auctions; company says it avoided bids below its cost threshold.
Adani framework: first-year order around 1.2 GW; RFQ for next 1.2 GW received, order expected to close around October or early November 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why have the new projects not started and what is the reason for delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said three PSU projects (one Coal India, two NTPC) did not get final NTP because PPAs were unsigned, and four international NTPs slipped on financing; only the Egypt Minya project has started.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for overheads and the Reliance order timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Recurring overheads are flat at about INR79-84 crores a quarter, about 5.5% of revenue now and expected near 4.5% for FY27; Reliance-related overhead increase is expected to be minimal as site costs sit in project budgets. Management gave no firm date for Reliance orders beyond 'some good news soon'.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company still expect 10% growth and EBITDA margin of 4-4.5%, and what are O&M targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed up to 10% growth and called 4-4.5% EBITDA margin a minimum requirement; O&M revenue is expected above INR400 crores in FY27. Egypt project margin is above 8% on a turnkey basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the guidance described as maintained when it was earlier 10-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the range was 10-15%, it now expects around 10% (not 0-1%), excluding Reliance, with possible support from international projects.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs rise despite lower execution?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited interest on newly availed credit lines and longer LC tenors being booked as interest; gross borrowings fell but cash balances declined, so net debt was steady.

qa_highlights.question: Banking limits, BGs and credit rating?
qa_highlights.answer: Over INR4,600 crores of new credit lines added across FY26 and FY27 to date plus over INR700 crores of surety bonds; utilisation about 70%. Rating under renewal; upgrade to be sought after Reliance or other large orders.

qa_highlights.question: O&M business model, margins and international expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the 18.9 GW O&M book is from own EPC contracts and 50% third-party; O&M is labour intensive with minimal overheads, gross margin about 20%, and O&M is about 5% of revenue, potentially rising to 10%. Focus geographies are Africa, Saudi Arabia, and Europe.

risks_watch: Execution timing: four domestic and four overseas projects not yet started; Q3/Q4 revenue ramp depends on NTPs, PPAs and financing of counterparties.
Guidance credibility: up to 10% FY27 growth requires a strong H2; analysts flagged risk of later downgrade.
Working capital: receivable days rose to 176 from 138 and net working capital is negative INR301 crores; monitor collections.
Domestic pricing pressure from low-priced reverse auction bids and ALMM-II cell shortages raising costs 15-17%.
Reliance and Adani order inflows are unconfirmed; Reliance timing and size not given.
Credit rating under renewal; banking and BG capacity at about 70% utilisation.
Nigeria EXIM project remains uncertain with no timeline committed.
key_quotes: Unfortunately, the Coal India and the 2 NTPC projects, because of the PPAs not being signed with the utilities, the final NTP did not come to us
So, basically, we are pretty confident of our ability to execute the projects.
It's not 0%, not between 0% and 1%. It will be around 10%.
I can't commit to the timeline at this moment for this project.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the medium-term order book and FY27 guidance, but cautious and at times evasive on timing: it would not give dates for Reliance orders or the Nigeria EXIM project, and it attributed the delays to PPAs, financing and NTPs. It conceded that Q2 results were weak, and it did not clearly explain why the 10% growth guidance was described as maintained when the earlier range was 10-15%.

adds.what: West Minya solar + storage project in Egypt (1,000 MW AC solar + 600 MWh BESS, ~USD 560m, 50:50 JV) - EPC execution, not company-owned capacity

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance is up to 10% growth (management later said roughly 10%, excluding Reliance orders), held despite H1 revenue down ~11%; backed by a INR12,481 crore order book and INR3,626 crore H1 inflow, but international execution has stalled with 8 projects not started due to delayed NTPs, so the guide relies on a strong Q3/Q4.
